FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A02
With ordinary brakes on a slippery road you squeeze gently and ease off if the wheels lock, but with anti-lock brakes you hold steady pressure and never pump [A02].
Why it matters: group braking technique; difficulty high; prereq sec09-F23; confusables sec09-F23, sec09-F24
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A02
Skid prevention relies on gentle speed reduction, while skid recovery forbids braking altogether and depends on steering toward the intended path [A02].
Why it matters: group skids; difficulty medium; prereq sec09-F21; confusables sec09-F23, sec09-F25
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A03
A brief anti-lock light at start up is normal, while a light that stays lit while driving means the anti-lock function is lost even though normal braking remains [A03].
Why it matters: group anti-lock brakes; difficulty low; prereq sec09-F27; confusables sec09-F28, sec09-F29
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A03
The clock rule puts headlights on from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, while the visibility rule requires them any time persons or vehicles cannot be seen five hundred feet ahead [A03].
Why it matters: group headlight law; difficulty medium; prereq sec09-F32; confusables sec09-F32, sec09-F08
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A03
High beams belong on open country roads with few vehicles, while low beams are required when meeting, following, under streetlights or in fog, and daytime running lights are neither [A03].
Why it matters: group headlight beams; difficulty medium; prereq sec09-F34; confusables sec09-F34, sec09-F30
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A01
Four wheel and all wheel drive give better traction in snow but no advantage on ice, which is why the winter following distance rises above four seconds for every vehicle [A01].
Why it matters: group winter traction; difficulty low; prereq sec09-F14; confusables sec09-F14, sec09-F26
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0048]
